findings.title: Chat template looks like a template-injection payload
findings.explanation: The model's Jinja chat template reaches Python internals (dunder attributes, os/subprocess, eval). Some runtimes render templates in an unsandboxed environment, which turns this into code execution (CVE-2024-34359 class).
findings.fix: Replace the chat template with a reviewed one and render templates in a sandboxed Jinja environment.

findings.title: Model file format can't be scanned yet
findings.explanation: This file is a format that can run code on load, but Gapproof can't parse this variant yet, so it can't be shown safe.
findings.fix: Convert to safetensors or GGUF, or document the file as an accepted risk.

findings.title: Model config requires remote code
findings.explanation: The Hugging Face config declares auto_map, so loading it with trust_remote_code=True imports and runs Python modules shipped with the model.
findings.fix: Vendor the model code into your own source tree, remove auto_map, and load with trust_remote_code=False.

findings.title: Keras model contains a Lambda layer
findings.explanation: Lambda layers store serialized Python bytecode that runs when the model is loaded (CVE-2024-3660 class).
findings.fix: Replace Lambda layers with registered custom layers defined in your source code, and load with safe_mode=True.

findings.title: Keras config references a non-Keras module
findings.explanation: The model config asks the loader to import objects from a module outside Keras. Config-driven imports have been used to bypass safe_mode (CVE-2025-1550 class).
findings.fix: Rebuild the model so its config only references Keras objects and your own registered classes.

findings.title: NumPy array stores Python objects
findings.explanation: An object-dtype .npy needs np.load(allow_pickle=True), which unpickles its payload. Any imports in that payload are reported separately.

evidence.detail: dtype object: payload is a pickle

findings.fix: Store numeric arrays only (no object dtype), or move the data to safetensors.

findings.title: Model file runs code when loaded
findings.explanation: Loading this pickle (pickle.load, joblib.load, or torch.load with weights_only=False) imports a code-execution primitive. Anyone who can change this file can run arbitrary code on the host that loads it.
findings.fix: Convert the weights to safetensors (or GGUF) and ship only that file. Don't load this file anywhere until it is replaced.

findings.title: ONNX model reads data from outside its directory
findings.explanation: An ONNX tensor's external_data location is absolute or climbs out of the model directory, so loading the model reads an arbitrary file from the host.
findings.fix: Re-export the model with external data stored beside it (relative paths only).

findings.title: Model file could not be verified
findings.explanation: Gapproof couldn't fully parse this model file (corrupt, truncated, over a safety limit, or deliberately malformed). It fails closed: an unverifiable model file is a finding, not a skip.
findings.fix: Re-export the file with its framework's serializer and rescan. If the file is legitimately unusual, document it as an accepted risk.

findings.title: ONNX external data file is missing
findings.explanation: The model references an external data file that isn't in the scanned filesystem, so its weights aren't accounted for in the AI-BOM.
findings.fix: Ship the external data file in the image, or point --models at its location.

findings.title: Model archive is structurally suspicious
findings.explanation: The archive has properties that make different readers see different content (for example duplicate member names). Scanners and loaders may disagree about what is inside.
findings.fix: Re-save the model with the framework's own serializer and rescan.

findings.title: Model file hides what it imports
findings.explanation: This pickle builds an import from values Gapproof can't resolve statically (computed STACK_GLOBAL operands or the copyreg extension registry). Legitimate serializers don't do this; obfuscated payloads do.
findings.fix: Treat the file as hostile and replace it with a safetensors export from a trusted source.
